rule: HRV baseline (mean and SD of ln rMSSD for the SWC band) uses the last 60 days
summary: The HRV-guided trials used shorter references: a 10-day rolling mean-SD (Kiviniemi) or a 4-week baseline block (Javaloyes, Vesterinen), and the methodological meta-analysis says the best way to set baseline values (fixed vs rolling, length) is still unresolved. A 60-day window gives a steadier band but lags real fitness-driven HRV shifts during a running ramp; the trials test the approach, not the 60-day number. Reasonable and conservative; label as heuristic.

sources.note: Used a 10-day rolling reference (mean - SD), much shorter than 60 days, and the HRV-guided group improved more
4 baseline weeks set each cyclist's resting HRV reference before HRV-guided training; improvements in TT and peak power
Individual SWC derived from a baseline period of a few weeks; HRV-guided group improved 3000 m
Meta-analysis: methods for baseline reference values (fixed vs rolling) 'require further study'; benefits small
